title: WPSB/379/2014 of GOVIND RAM JAISWAL Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
Reserved on: 16.12.2025
 Delivered on: 05.01.2026
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
WRIT PETITION (S/B) No. 379 of 2014
Govind Ram Jaiswal ......Petitioner
Versus
State of Uttarakhand
And Another .......Respondents
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Mr. Vinay Kumar, learned counsel for the petitioner.
Mr. P.S. Bisht, learned Addl. C.S.C. for the State.
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Coram: Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J.
 Hon'ble Alok Mahra, J.
Per: Alok Mahra, J.
Petitioner was appointed on a Group B post in
pay-scale of 8000-13500 in Uttar Pradesh Educational
(General Services) in hill sub-cadre through direct
recruitment pursuant to the selection held by the Uttar
Pradesh Public Service Commission. Pursuant to his
selection, he was posted as Principal, Government Inter-College, Dhaund, District Pauri Garhwal vide order dated
27.09.1999. At the time of the appointment of the
petitioner, the service conditions of the post on which the
petitioner was appointed was governed by Uttar Pradesh
Educational (General Education Cadre) Service Rules,
1992.
2. After reorganization of State of Uttar Pradesh,

the Central Government issued an order dated
11.09.2001, whereby members of hill sub-cadre were
automatically allotted to the State of Uttarakhand. As
such, petitioner was allotted State of Uttarakhand.
3. Secretary Finance, Government of Uttarakhand
issued a Government Order on 20.12.2001, whereby, the
5th Central Pay Commission was implemented in respect
of Teachers/Principals of Primary and Secondary
Institutions. The ordinary pay-scale of Principal with
grade pay of Rs. 8000-13500 was enhanced notionally to
Rs. 10000-15200 w.e.f. 01.01.1996 and actual payment
was to be made w.e.f. 01.07.2001. Pursuant to this
Government Order, petitioner was also placed in the pay-scale of 10,000-15200.
4. The State notified the Uttaranchal Educational
(General Education Cadre) Service Rules, 2006 vide
notification dated 19.06.2006. The cadre of service
comprised of Group A and Group B posts in the
Educational Department. The post of Principal,
Government Inter College getting pay-scale of 10,000-
15,200 was placed at senior pay-scale grade II.
5. As per Rule 5(v) of the Uttaranchal Educational
(General Education Cadre) Service Rules, 2006, the post
of Principal, Government Inter-College and Deputy
Director, Headquarters was placed on the same pay-scale

i.e. 10,000-15,200.
6. Vide order dated 11.12.2008, petitioner was
posted as Deputy Director, Directorate of School
Education, Dehradun against vacant post.
7. That vide Government Order dated 01.03.2009,
recommendation of 6th Pay Commission was made
applicable in the Education Department w.e.f.
01.01.2006. The pay-scale of 10,000-15,200 was
upgraded to pay band-3, 15,600-34,100 with grade pay of
7600 w.e.f. 01.01.2006.
8. That another Government Order dated
11.03.2011 was issued which provided that the pay-scale
of 10,650-15,850 and 10,000-15,200 was revised to
15,600-39,100 with grade pay 7600 w.e.f. 01.01.2006. In
pursuance of this, petitioner was placed in this revised
pay-scale of 15600-39100 with grade pay 7600.
9. That vide Government Order dated 14.06.2011,
the School Education Department was restructured. After
re-structuring of the department, 297 posts were
restructured into administrative cadre. The
administrative cadre consisted of 297 posts, out of which,
40 posts of Deputy Directors in the pay-scale of 15,600-
39,100 grade pay 7600 were created and 97 posts of
Block Education Officer/equivalent posts in the pay scale
of Rs. 15600-39100 with grade pay of Rs. 6600/- were

created. After re-structuring of the department, options
were invited from the Principal and other officers serving
in the Education Department regarding their choice to
serve in Education cadre or in Administrative cadre.
10. Petitioner, who was posted as Deputy Director,
Education gave his option for administrative cadre. An
office-memorandum was issued by the State Government
on 25.06.2012, whereby, list of members of
administrative cadre and education cadre was published.
The name of the petitioner figured at Serial No. 12 in the
list of members of administrative cadre. Vide notification
dated 20.12.2013, the Uttarakhand State Educational
(Administrative Cadre) Service Rules, 2013 were notified.
11. An office-memorandum dated 10.01.2014 was
issued whereby members of administrative cadre were
transferred. By this order, petitioner was transferred from
the post of Deputy Director in the Directorate of
Secondary Education to the post of Block Education
Officer. As per the Uttarakhand State Educational
(Administrative Cadre) Service Rules, 2013, the post of
Block Education Officer carries pay-scale of 15,600-
39,100, grade pay 6600, while petitioner was serving in
pay-scale 15,600-39,100, grade pay 7600.
12. Petitioner filed a writ petition challenging his
transfer order and by means of the interim order, the

transfer order in respect of petitioner was stayed by this
Court. Respondent no. 1 issued Government Order dated
07.07.2014, whereby employees who have opted for the
administrative cadre were absorbed in the administrative
cadre. Petitioner was absorbed in the post of Block
Education Officer though the Government Order provided
that the employees who are getting higher salary and are
absorbed in the lower pay-scale will continue to get the
present pay-scale as they are presently paid until they
are promoted in the present pay-scale.
13. By means of the present writ petition,
petitioner has challenged this Government Order wherein
he has been absorbed in the lower post of Block
Education Officer carrying grade pay 6600 whereas he
was posted as Deputy Director, Education in the grade
pay of 7600. Beside this, petitioner has also prayed that
he be granted benefit of 1st ACP after completing ten
years of regular, continuous and satisfactory service in
the pay scale of Rs. 37,400-67000 with grade pay of Rs.
8700/- in terms of the Government Order dated
01.07.2013 w.e.f. 10.12.2009. Petitioner has further
prayed for his candidature for promotion on the post of
Joint Director Education in terms of mandate of Service
Rules of 2013.
14. The petitioner was sent on deputation in the

Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises and
was relieved vide office memo dated 10.07.2014. In this
order also, the designation of the petitioner was
mentioned as Deputy Director and his pay-scale was also
mentioned as 15,600-39,100 with grade pay 7600.
Furthermore, after completion of his deputation period,
petitioner was allowed to join Deputy Director, School
Education vide order dated 12.10.2017 by the Joint
Secretary, Secondary Education Department. The
Director General of Schools have issued communications
to the Secretary, School Education on 05.05.2018
wherein he has submitted the fact that petitioner was
serving on the pay-scale of 15600-39100 grade pay 7600
w.e.f. 01.01.2006. Despite this, he was absorbed on the
post of Block Education Officer in grade pay of Rs. 6600
and he has requested that the Government Order dated
07.07.2014 be amended and petitioner be absorbed on
the post of Deputy Director.
15. Learned counsel for the petitioner has
submitted that absorption of the petitioner on the lower
post amounts to reduction in rank and entails civil
consequences, inasmuch as, as per the Uttarakhand
State Educational (Administrative Cadre) Service Rules,
2013, the feeding cadre for the post of Deputy Director is
Block Education Officer, who have completed four years

of service in that post. Learned counsel has further
submitted that since he was already getting the salary in
the grade pay of 7600 and was working on the post of
Deputy Director Education at the time when options were
invited as such he could not have been absorbed in the
lower post.
16. Per contra, learned counsel for the State has
submitted that the absorption order clearly stipulates
that the employees who are getting higher salary and are
absorbed in the lower pay-scale will continue to get the
present pay-scale as they are presently paid until they
are promoted in the present pay-scale. Learned counsel
further submitted that petitioner was only made In-charge Deputy Director and was not posted on a regular
basis.
17. Heard learned counsel for the parties and
perused the record.
18. A bare perusal of the transfer order dated
11.12.2008 would reveal that it was a regular transfer
and it nowhere mentions that it is only a makeshift or a
temporary arrangement.
19. After re-structuring, 40 posts of Deputy
Directors were created and since more than 40 persons
had opted for the said post and these 40 posts of Deputy
Director were filled as per the seniority of the employees,

who had given their options to serve in the administrative
department, therefore, petitioner's services were absorbed
on the post of Block Education Officer.
20. When the matter was heard before the
Coordinate Bench on 06.06.2024, learned counsel for the
petitioner has submitted that out of the 40 posts, only 33
posts of Deputy Director were filled and 7 posts remained
unfilled and the Coordinate Bench has directed the State
to get instructions in this regard, but, even today, when
the matter was heard finally, the State Counsel has no
instructions in this regard. Be that as it may, since, the
petitioner was appointed on the post of Principal, Inter-College in the year 1999 by direct recruitment in the pay-scale which was equivalent to that of Deputy Director and
was also transferred from the post of Principal to the post
of Deputy Director. Petitioner was sent on deputation
wherein his designation was mentioned as Deputy
Director, Secondary Education and after completion of
his deputation, he was permitted to join on the post of
Deputy Director, Education.
21. Taking into consideration the above facts, this
Court is of the considered view that absorption of the
petitioner on a lower post of Block Education Officer
cannot be sustained, as an employee serving on a higher
post cannot be absorbed on a lower post. Hence, the

Government Order dated 07.07.2014 insofar as it relates
to the petitioner, is liable to be quashed and is hereby
quashed. The respondents are directed to absorb the
petitioner on the post of Deputy Director w.e.f.
07.07.2014 alongwith all consequential benefits.
22. With the above observation, the writ petition
stands disposed of.
(Alok Mahra, J.) (Ravindra Maithani, J.)
 05.01.2026
Ujjwal
